answer: Progressive registration fees resist sybils: the non-refundable fee to mint a new identity rises with the count of identities already traced to a funding source, so the first account is cheap and the hundredth is punishing. A ferrous-heavy curve charges each new vertex off one wallet more than the last; an opal-smooth lone honest join pays the floor. An attacker spinning many identities from one purse climbs the fee ramp per head, so mass creation is priced super-linearly while a single genuine agent is barely taxed.
